summary: An educational app that describes the logistics of maintaining and managing resources in a Martian space base. It explains ideas in a way that is not too simple to where there are too many details missing, but not too complicated so that a young student using the app can understand.
details: The app considers 4 main metrics: Oxygen, Power, Food, and Crew Health. Enabling Solar Arrays and burning trash into methane gives power, oxygen generators make oxygen, hydroponic farms make food, and radiation shielding protects the crew from radiation poisoning, which maintains their health. When one of these modules is enabled, power is used. And if too much power is used, the modules cannot function, which eventually could lead to lack of oxygen or food, so it enables precise decision making. It displays visuals and cues in a cartoonish way that caters to young children. It is meant to educate children about Martian bases and the necessities required to let them thrive, as well as supporting precise decision making and and critical thinking. Google AI Studio was used for the programming, and the coding languages used were TypeScript for the game itself, and HTML as well as Tailwind CSS for the visuals and layout. The project includes fun features so children are more engaged, like occasional fun facts, character selection, and difficulty modes. We considered the thinking of the users of the app as well as the reality of the aspects in the game compared to actual NASA research.
